title: Find in Mountain Array
description:
(This problem is an interactive problem.)

An array `arr` is a **mountain array** if and only if:
- `arr.length >= 3`
- There exists some index `i` with `0 < i < arr.length - 1` such that:
  - `arr[0] < arr[1] < ... < arr[i - 1] < arr[i]`
  - `arr[i] > arr[i + 1] > ... > arr[arr.length - 1]`

Given a mountain array `mountainArr` and an integer `target`, return the **minimum** `index` such that `mountainArr.get(index) == target`. If such an `index` does not exist, return `-1`.

You cannot access the mountain array directly. You may only access the array using a `MountainArray` interface:
- `MountainArray.get(k)` returns the element of the array at index `k` (0-indexed).
- `MountainArray.length()` returns the length of the array.

Submissions making more than **100 calls** to `MountainArray.get` will be judged wrong.
constraints: mountainArr is guaranteed to be a valid mountain array.
hints: Use three binary searches so that you make at most ~3 * log2(n) <= 45 calls to MountainArray.get, well within the 100-call budget.
First, binary search on [1, n - 2] comparing get(mid) and get(mid + 1) to locate the peak index.

Next, binary search the strictly increasing left side [0, peak] first (since you need the minimum index). Only if target is not found there, binary search the strictly decreasing right side [peak + 1, n - 1].

examples.explanation: Target 3 appears at index 2 and index 5. The minimum index is 2.
Target 3 does not exist in [0, 1, 2, 4, 2, 1], so return -1.
Target 2 appears on the descending side at index 2.

inputs.name: mountainArr
inputs.description: Underlying mountain array (accessed only via MountainArray API)
